summary: The primary decision record on what cross-frame divergence means: formally DEFERRED, blocked by DECISION-02, since choosing an aggregation algorithm now would hide an ontological decision about frames. Lays out majority (aggregate, unresolved equal-frame-weight assumption) vs intraframe-only (refuse, requires a new BoundaryCondition and blocks determination) as the two surviving alternatives; discovers via a new witness C7 (frame-refinement invariance) that majority's verdict changes when the SAME evidence is merely recorded at finer timestamp resolution -- a constitutive defect (frame count is an artefact of recording resolution) of the same shape as last-wins's order-dependence; explicitly WITHDRAWS this lane's own earlier [PROP] preference for intraframe-only on C7 grounds as an inference that outran its premises (the argument treated 'non-evidential' as already settled); and opens a third possibility (developed in DECISION-02 §5): stop requiring composition to manufacture a frame-free Standing at all.

It also introduces, as a live third possibility, abandoning the requirement that composition produce a frame-free Standing at all, developed further in the companion DECISION-02 document (S2508, same batch).

summary: DECISION-02, blocking Z-DECISION-cross-frame-divergence: poses whether phi identifies semantically meaningful evaluation frames (Option B) or merely organizes evidence as a representational partition (Option A); under A, majority violates DECISION-01 constitutively (counts representational boundaries, making representation granularity semantically observable -- a stronger objection than merely assuming equal frame weights); under B, majority does not violate C7 but still owes an unestablished basis for equal frame weighting. Lays out a five-step decision procedure D1-D5 and keeps open a third architecture-neutral option: stop requiring composition to manufacture a frame-free Standing at all, instead keeping frame-relative standings plus an explicit divergence marker with a separate later determination step.

summary: An HPA advisory reconciliation strategy for Theory v1.1 -> v1.2: introduces a four-layer distinction (Philosophical/Epistemic-Mathematical/DDD-Domain/Architectural) with a rule that no concept may drop a layer without a declared bridge; specifies eight critical reclassifications (K_t from operational to representational/candidate; Equality from implicit to first-class unresolved; Observation from defined to open; Buddhi from architecture to lens; Zero from primitive to candidate construct; Sarathi from domain object to design lens; Transformation from defined to candidate; E_t vs K_t as a new open research distinction); proposes an 11-item epistemic status vocabulary (ESTABLISHED/DERIVED/BOUNDED/HYPOTHESIS/INTERPRETATION/CORROBORATION/NORMATIVE/TECHNICALLY-OPEN/DEFERRED/REFUTED/UNKNOWN); lists what v1.1 elements survive unchanged; and lays out a twelve-part v1.2 structural outline plus a full reconciliation-prompt template.
contribution_assessment: This document resolves an apparent corpus inconsistency flagged while processing S2499/S2500/S2501: those documents used an 11-tuple K_t=(A_t,R_t,E_t,Sigma_t,H_t,Z_t,L_t,T_t,G_t,C_t,M_t) that did not match this batch's v1.2 A_t=Gamma(E_t,Q,C,EC) experiments. This reconciliation document shows that 11-tuple IS the actual v1.1 formulation, and v1.2 explicitly reclassifies it as merely a 'candidate representation' with operational semantics left open -- meaning S2499-S2501 were carrying forward v1.1-era vocabulary without applying the v1.2 epistemic-status qualifiers this document specifies, rather than inventing an unrelated formulation.

summary: An HPA advisory ratifying 'Gap Theory v1.0': defines the epistemic gap set-theoretically as Delta_t={r in R_t : not Sat(K_t,r)} (rather than a heterogeneous I_t-K_t difference), a three-level hierarchy (semantic Delta_t, typed Delta_t^typed with 10 gap-class tags G1-G10, numerical G_t=sum(w_r*d_r) as a derived view), the theorem Zero_t iff Delta_t=empty iff K_t models EC_t, and Progress as set inclusion K_{t+1}>=_EC K_t iff Delta_{t+1} subseteq Delta_t; recommends freezing these core definitions and the 10 gap classes (as tags, not mutually-exclusive categories) while leaving Sat(K_t,r)'s per-class definition as the open bridge problem and the universal type of K_t as out of scope.
contribution_assessment: This document's headline recommendation to FREEZE 'Zero_t iff Delta_t=empty' as an established theorem directly contradicts the main research lane's actual v1.2 finding (documented in this same batch's S2480/S2481, and the earlier Phase 5 boundary-object work): that Zero<=>Delta=empty 'becomes ambiguous' under three-valued Sat and was explicitly RETIRED in favor of closure defined over the boundary object 𝓑, repairing D-0 6/6 under all three contradiction models. Neither document references or resolves the other; the corpus contains both the advisory recommendation to freeze this exact equivalence and the executed research finding that retires it.

summary: An extraction from Ziem's 'Frames of Understanding in Text and Discourse' (cognitive frame semantics) mapped to KnowledgeOS: frames as slot/filler/default-value schemas evoked by linguistic input; the U-relevance postulate (no distinction relevant to understanding may be excluded on methodological grounds) mapped directly to R_req; the holistic-vs-modularist semantics debate resolved in favor of holism (no linguistic/encyclopaedic knowledge split); evocation (form-triggered) vs invocation (interpreter-triggered) frame activation; hyperonym type reduction as a systematic method for determining slots; entrenchment (token/type frequency) as the mechanism by which default values and basic-level categories emerge; and a generic-frame method for metaphor/analogy analysis via shared slots of source and target frames.
contribution_assessment: This extraction belongs to the same 'Gap Theory' thread as S2513 (it explicitly maps Contr to gap-class G5 and restates Zero=Delta-empty as a confirmed KnowledgeOS concept, using that thread's vocabulary rather than the main lane's careful three-model/boundary-object treatment of Zero). Its most substantively new content for KnowledgeOS is the U-relevance postulate (a strong independent formal principle for R_req: any representation collapsing an understanding-relevant distinction is inadequate regardless of elegance) and the slot/filler/default-value frame structure as a candidate model for evaluation representation and boundary metadata.
